observation.visible_scene: A transparent cylindrical glass partially filled with water stands on a wooden tabletop in front of a black-and-white checkerboard sheet mounted on a cardboard panel. The camera and background remain fixed throughout. The glass, seen through refraction, shows the checkerboard as stretched horizontal dark/light bands, with a vertical column-edge distortion line visible inside the water.
visible_changes: The water glass translates slowly and steadily leftward across the frame, from a right-of-center position at t=0.0s to a near-center position by t=1.6s, while its size, water level, and orientation stay constant.

As the glass shifts left over the static checkerboard, the refracted horizontal bands inside it slide and re-align, and the vertical distortion line (a refracted column edge) moves across the interior of the glass, appearing as a wavy/diagonal streak at times (e.g., t=0.12-0.16, t=0.44-0.48, t=0.80-0.84, t=1.12-1.16, t=1.40-1.44).
The checkerboard pattern outside the glass and the cardboard edges do not move, confirming the leftward motion belongs to the glass, not the camera.
outside_clip_unknowns: No hand or operator is visible, so how the glass is moved is not shown.
The motion is already in progress at the first frame and continues past the last; no start or stop of the movement is captured.
What lies beyond the cropped segment (further translation or rest) is not visible.
uncertain_details: The vertical streak inside the water is a refracted image of a checkerboard column edge, not a separate object inside the glass.
The exact speed of the glass is slow and roughly uniform within the excerpt, but precise velocity is not measurable from sampled frames.
Minor frame-to-frame jitter in the streak shape reflects changing refraction as the glass moves, not deformation of the glass.
